A demand-side platform (DSP) is a technology platform used in digital advertising to manage and optimize the buying process of ad inventory across multiple ad exchanges and supply sources. It provides advertisers and agencies with a centralized system to purchase and manage digital ad placements in real-time auctions. DSPs use sophisticated algorithms and data-driven insights to help advertisers target specific audiences, optimize ad performance, and achieve their campaign goals efficiently. DSP Advertising refers to the practice of using a DSP to execute programmatic ad buying, where advertisers can leverage audience data, targeting options, and real-time bidding capabilities to deliver relevant and targeted ads to the right users, at the right time, and in the most cost-effective manner. DSP Advertising empowers advertisers to reach their desired audiences across a wide range of websites, apps and other digital channels, while providing them with comprehensive control, insights, and flexibility in their ad campaigns.
What are some examples of DSP Advertising?

There are several examples of demand-side platform (DSP) advertising that showcase its versatility and effectiveness in reaching target audiences. For instance, a retail brand may use a DSP to run a programmatic ad campaign targeting consumers who have shown interest in similar products or have visited their website recently. The DSP enables the brand to bid on ad placements in real-time auctions, ensuring that the ads are delivered to the right users across various traditional ad channels, like Display and Mobile, and emerging channels like Connected TV, Streaming Audio, Digital Out-of-Home and more. Similarly, a travel company could leverage a DSP to target specific demographics and geographical locations, delivering personalized ads to potential travelers who are more likely to engage with their offerings. Additionally, a financial institution could use a DSP to reach out to individuals who have displayed an interest in financial planning or investment-related content, allowing the institution to promote its services effectively. In all these cases, DSP advertising offers precise targeting, real-time optimization, and comprehensive insights capabilities to drive successful ad campaigns.
What omnichannel marketing services does Viant offer?

Viant is a leading provider of omnichannel marketing services, offering a comprehensive suite of solutions to help brands and advertisers maximize their reach and engagement across various traditional and emerging ad channels, such as Connected TV (CTV), Streaming Audio, In-Game and more. Our services encompass audience targeting, cross-device identity resolution, data management, and programmatic advertising. Viant enables advertisers to leverage their first-party and third-party data to create detailed audience segments and target them across display, video, mobile, and connected TV platforms. Our cross-device identity resolution capabilities ensure that advertisers can recognize and engage with consumers seamlessly across multiple devices, providing a cohesive and personalized user experience. Viant's data management platform (DMP) allows advertisers to organize, analyze, and activate their data effectively, enabling precise audience targeting and campaign optimization. Furthermore, Viant's programmatic advertising solutions enable automated ad buying and real-time bidding, delivering targeted messages to the right audiences at the right time. Overall, Viant's omnichannel DSP solutions provide advertisers with the tools and insights needed to drive impactful and cohesive marketing campaigns across the digital landscape.
What are the benefits of using Viant's DSP?

Using Viant's DSP offers several key benefits for advertisers. Firstly, it provides access to a vast array of inventory across multiple channels and devices, allowing advertisers to reach their target audiences efficiently. Secondly, Viant's DSP leverages advanced data capabilities, enabling precise audience targeting and optimization, resulting in higher campaign effectiveness. Additionally, the self-service platform provides advertisers with transparency, control, and real-time insights into campaign performance, empowering them to make data-driven decisions and optimize their advertising strategies effectively. Overall, Viant's DSP offers a powerful and comprehensive solution for advertisers seeking to maximize their reach, engagement, and return on investment in the programmatic advertising space.
Why are Demand Side Platforms important?

Demand-side platforms (DSPs) are important in the world of digital advertising for several reasons. Firstly, DSPs provide advertisers with access to a vast ecosystem of ad inventory across multiple publishers, ad exchanges, and supply sources. This allows advertisers to reach their target audiences at scale and with precision. Secondly, DSPs utilize sophisticated algorithms and data-driven insights to optimize ad campaigns in real-time, ensuring that ad impressions are served to the most relevant users, thereby maximizing the effectiveness of advertising budgets. Lastly, DSPs provide advertisers with comprehensive control, transparency, and reporting capabilities, enabling them to track and evaluate campaign performance, make data-driven decisions, and continually refine their advertising strategies. Overall, DSPs play a crucial role in enabling efficient and targeted programmatic advertising, driving better audience reach, engagement, and return on investment for advertisers.
What’s the difference between DSP and SSP?

The main difference between a demand-side platform (DSP) and a supply-side platform (SSP) lies in their respective roles and perspectives within the programmatic advertising ecosystem. DSPs are used by advertisers and agencies to purchase and manage ad inventory, targeting specific audiences and optimizing ad performance. On the other hand, SSPs are utilized by publishers to manage and sell their ad inventory, connecting with multiple demand sources including DSPs to maximize revenue. While DSPs focus on buying ad placements, SSPs concentrate on selling ad placements, creating a seamless connection between supply and demand sides of the programmatic advertising marketplace.
How do demand-side platforms work?

A demand-side platform (DSP) is a software service that allows advertisers to buy digital ad inventory across multiple exchanges in real time. Using automated bidding, DSPs help advertisers target specific audiences based on data signals like demographics, behaviors and device usage. This helps to ensure ads are shown to the right people at the right time, optimizing performance and budget efficiency.
How does Viant’s DSP stand out from other demand-side platforms?

Viant’s DSP differentiates itself with its people-based targeting approach, leveraging first-party data and identity resolution to enhance precision. It provides cookieless solutions , advanced AI-driven campaign optimization via ViantAI and seamless integrations with leading data providers. Additionally, Viant offers transparent reporting and omnichannel capabilities, helping to ensure advertisers maximize reach and ROI.
What kind of measurement and reporting tools does Viant’s DSP offer?

Viant’s DSP provides robust measurement tools, including real-time reporting, attribution modeling and offline-to-online impact analysis. It supports cross-channel insights , audience segmentation performance, and incrementality measurement to track ad effectiveness. With advanced analytics, advertisers can optimize campaigns with greater accuracy and transparency.
What is real-time bidding (RTB), and how does it work in a DSP?

Real-time bidding (RTB) is an automated process where digital ad inventory is bought and sold in milliseconds through an auction. When a user visits a website or app, a bid request is sent, and DSPs analyze the available data to determine if and how much to bid. The highest bidder wins, and their ad is instantly displayed, helping to ensure cost-efficient and highly targeted ad placements.
Does Viant’s DSP offer cross-device targeting?

Yes, Viant’s DSP enables cross-device targeting, allowing advertisers to reach users across multiple devices, including desktops, mobile phones, tablets and CTV. By leveraging identity resolution and deterministic matching, Viant helps to ensure seamless ad experiences while maintaining accuracy in attribution and audience targeting.
Is Viant’s DSP self-serve, managed or both?

Viant’s DSP offers both self-serve and managed service options. Advertisers can take full control of their campaigns with the self-serve platform, or they can leverage Viant’s team of experts for hands-on management and optimization. This flexibility allows brands and agencies to choose the best approach for their needs.
How do I get started with Viant’s demand-side platform?

Getting started is easy — simply contact Viant to request a demo or set up an account. Our team will guide you through the onboarding process, help define campaign goals, and provide training on the platform. Whether you choose self-serve or managed service, Viant’s support team will help to ensure a smooth and effective launch.
How does Viant measure offline conversions or in-store visits?

Viant measures offline conversions and in-store visits by leveraging its proprietary Household ID™ technology and a robust identity graph. By connecting digital ad exposure to real-world locations and validated visitation data from partners like SafeGraph and Veraset, Viant can provide detailed "Foot Traffic Attribution" reports. Additionally, the platform allows advertisers to ingest their own first-party data—such as email lists or transaction records—which are matched against the Household ID to provide closed-loop reporting. To ensure accuracy, Viant uses a "ghost bidding" methodology to create control groups, enabling marketers to see the incremental lift and true ROI of their digital campaigns on physical retail sales.
How quickly can a campaign go live on Viant’s DSP?

With the launch of ViantAI, the timeline for taking a campaign live has been reduced from days to moments. While traditional programmatic planning and setup often involve manual processes that can take several business days, Viant’s AI-powered planning tool can generate a data-driven media plan in as little as 60 seconds based on basic inputs like budget, audience, and goals. Once the plan is generated, it can be seamlessly activated within the Viant DSP with the push of a button. This automation streamlines the transition from strategy to execution, allowing advertisers to launch high-impact omnichannel campaigns almost instantly while still maintaining full control over creative approvals and final optimizations.
What role does artificial intelligence play in DSPs?

Artificial Intelligence serves as the central intelligence layer of a DSP, automating complex tasks that would be impossible to manage manually at scale. Within Viant’s platform, AI handles real-time bid optimization by analyzing millions of impressions per second to determine the ideal price for meeting specific KPIs like ROAS or eCPM. Beyond bidding, AI plays a critical role in media planning, fraud detection, and predictive audience segmentation, using machine learning to identify the users most likely to convert. By managing everything from frequency capping across devices to autonomous budget reallocation, AI allows marketers to shift their focus from tactical execution to high-level strategy, ensuring every dollar is spent on the most effective impressions.

It provides cookieless solutions, advanced AI-driven campaign optimization via ViantAI and seamless integrations with leading data providers. Additionally, Viant offers transparent reporting and omnichannel capabilities, helping to ensure advertisers maximize reach and ROI.

It supports cross-channel insights, audience segmentation performance, and incrementality measurement to track ad effectiveness. With advanced analytics, advertisers can optimize campaigns with greater accuracy and transparency.

WHAT IS PROGRAMMATIC ADVERTISING? Expand

Programmatic advertising refers to the automated buying and selling of digital ad inventory using technology and algorithms. It involves the use of demand-side platforms (DSPs) by advertisers to bid on and purchase ad impressions in real-time auctions, while supply-side platforms (SSPs) enable publishers to offer their ad inventory for sale. Programmatic advertising utilizes data, targeting options, and real-time optimization to deliver relevant ads to the right audience at the right time, making the ad buying process more efficient and effective. It allows for precise audience targeting, scalability, and improved campaign performance through automation and data-driven decision-making.
WHAT IS TARGETED ADVERTISING AND HOW DOES IT COMPARE TO PROGRAMMATIC? Expand

Targeted advertising refers to the practice of delivering ads to specific and relevant audiences based on people’s characteristics, behaviors, or preferences. It involves tailoring ad content and placement to reach a desired audience segment, increasing the relevance and effectiveness of the ads. Programmatic advertising, on the other hand, is a method of auction-based buying and selling ad inventory that utilizes automated technology and data-driven algorithms to optimize the ad buying process in real-time. While targeted advertising focuses on reaching specific audiences, programmatic advertising is a broader approach that leverages data, automation, and real-time bidding to deliver targeted ads efficiently and at scale. Programmatic advertising often incorporates targeted advertising techniques to maximize the precision and impact of ad campaigns.
HOW DOES PROGRAMMATIC ADVERTISING WORK? Expand

Programmatic advertising works through an automated process that involves various stakeholders and technologies. Advertisers use demand-side platforms (DSPs) to set campaign parameters, define target audiences, and determine bidding strategies. These DSPs then participate in real-time auctions (organized by Supply-side platforms (SSPs), where ad placements are bought and sold. SSPs enable publishers to make their ad inventory available for auction. When a user visits a website or app, placement becomes available and is instantly auctioned off among participating DSPs. The DSPs assess several data provided by the SSPs, including the audience data, such as demographics and browsing behavior, and place a bid on behalf of the advertiser. The highest bidding DSP wins the auction, and the applicable advertiser’s ad is instantly delivered to the user's device. This entire process takes place within milliseconds, allowing advertisers to deliver highly targeted ads in real-time to their desired audience.
WHAT ARE EXAMPLES OF PROGRAMMATIC ADVERTISING? Expand

There are several examples of programmatic advertising that demonstrate its diverse applications. For instance, a retail brand can leverage programmatic advertising to dynamically serve personalized product recommendations to individual users based on their browsing history or purchase behavior. A travel company can use programmatic advertising to target potential customers who have shown interest in vacation destinations, delivering tailored ads showcasing relevant travel deals. Additionally, a healthcare organization can utilize programmatic advertising to reach specific demographic groups with targeted messaging promoting preventive care services or health-related products. These examples highlight the versatility and effectiveness of programmatic advertising in delivering relevant and timely messages to the right audiences.
WHAT TYPES OF PROGRAMMATIC ADVERTISING SOLUTIONS DOES VIANT OFFER? Expand

Viant offers a range of programmatic advertising solutions designed to help advertisers achieve their campaign goals effectively. Viant’s offerings include access to a vast inventory across display, video, mobile, and connected TV platforms, allowing advertisers to reach their target audiences across multiple channels. Viant also provides advanced data capabilities, enabling precise audience targeting and optimization. Its self-service platform offers transparency, control, and real-time insights, empowering advertisers to make data-driven decisions and optimize their campaigns. Overall, Viant's programmatic advertising solutions encompass inventory access, audience targeting, data-driven optimization, and comprehensive campaign management tools.
WHAT ARE THE BENEFITS OF PROGRAMMATIC ADVERTISING? Expand

Programmatic advertising offers several key benefits for advertisers. Firstly, it enables precise targeting, allowing advertisers to reach specific audiences based on demographics, interests, and behaviors. This results in more relevant and personalized ad experiences for users. Secondly, programmatic advertising offers real-time optimization, allowing advertisers to adjust their campaigns in real-time based on performance data, maximizing their return on investment. Additionally, programmatic advertising automates the ad buying process, increasing efficiency and reducing manual effort. It also provides comprehensive reporting and insights, allowing advertisers to track and measure the success of their campaigns. Overall, programmatic advertising offers increased targeting precision, efficiency, and data-driven decision-making, leading to more effective and impactful ad campaigns.
WHAT’S THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN PROGRAMMATIC AND DISPLAY ADVERTISING? Expand

Programmatic advertising and display advertising are related but distinct concepts. Display advertising refers to the practice of delivering visual ads, such as banner ads or rich media ads, on websites or mobile apps. It encompasses the creative aspects of designing and delivering visual advertisements to target audiences. Programmatic advertising, on the other hand, refers to the automated buying and selling of digital ad inventory using technology and algorithms. It focuses on the process of ad buying, utilizing data, targeting options, and real-time optimization to deliver ads efficiently and at scale. While programmatic advertising can include display advertising, it extends beyond it by incorporating other ad formats and channels, like video, mobile, audio, digital out-of-home and connected TV, and employing advanced targeting and automation techniques.
